entry.title: GitHub Actions Cache Isolation [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Cache Isolation for GitHub Actions gives users and organizations the ability to create secure, partitioned cache environments for their workflows. This feature helps prevent accidental or malicious data leaks between workflows, offering fine-grained control and audit capabilities for enterprise-grade automation.

Expected Outcome

By isolating caches by repository, workflow, or branch, this update aims to eliminate risks like cache poisoning and data exfiltration, improving the security and reliability of CI/CD pipelines. Customers can expect more trustworthy and predictable workflow runs, with enhanced control over how and when caches are accessed or modified.

entry.title: Actions Runner Controller Release 0.14.1 [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With the Actions Runner Controller 0.14.1 release, platform teams and open source contributors can more easily manage self-hosted runners on Kubernetes. This update delivers quality-of-life improvements, clearer configuration, better troubleshooting, and incorporates valuable community contributions, making day-to-day operations smoother and more reliable.

Expected Outcome

We aim to reduce friction for teams operating and maintaining ARC by addressing community-reported issues and enhancing the developer experience. This release builds trust in the ARC release process and helps teams confidently migrate away from legacy solutions while benefiting from a more polished and stable platform.

entry.title: Scale Set Job To Runner Assignment [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With Scale Set Job To Runner Assignment, customers using GitHub Actions Scale Sets can automatically distribute jobs to the most suitable runners, making large-scale CI/CD workflows faster and more efficient. This feature reduces wait times and resource waste by ensuring jobs are assigned where they can run best, even as demand changes.

Expected Outcome

We want customers to experience smoother, more reliable automation at scale, with less manual intervention and fewer workflow bottlenecks. By improving job placement and scheduling, this release aims to help teams deliver software faster and more predictably.

entry.title: Release: Elevate Attestation as a First-Class Object in Repository UI and Security Overview [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now easily view and verify attestations directly in your repository’s UI and Security Overview, with clear SLSA level indicators. This makes it simpler for developers, security admins, and compliance leads to assess trust and compliance at a glance, streamlining your security workflows.

Expected Outcome

By making attestations a first-class part of the repository experience, we aim to reduce friction and increase adoption of secure development practices. This change helps enterprise teams meet SLSA source track requirements and strengthens trust in your software supply chain.

entry.title: SBOM Export user interface and API support retrieval of dependency snapshots [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub now lets you export and retrieve Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs,) including dependency snapshots, through both the UI and a fast, asynchronous API. Instead of generating SBOMs on demand (which was slow and subject to strict rate limits), SBOMs are now pre-stored for rapid retrieval, so you get reliable, consistent results even across large estates with tens of thousands of repositories. This makes it straightforward to integrate with third-party SCA tools, automate compliance reporting, and maintain internal audit records at scale.

Expected Outcome

Enterprise customers managing large codebases have been unable to programmatically traverse their full repository estate for SBOMs due to synchronous API limitations, aggressive rate limits, and no guarantee of a response for any given request. With this release, we resolve those pain points by delivering a redesigned backend that supports asynchronous retrieval of pre-built SBOMs, including artifact and snapshot-level granularity. The expected outcomes are: (1) customers can reliably export SBOMs at scale without hitting availability issues, (2) integration with external compliance and SCA tooling becomes seamless, and (3) GitHub strengthens its position as the default platform for end-to-end supply chain security.

entry.title: Users can now search their complete organization-wide dependencies [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Gain full visibility into every open source dependency across your organization — all in one place. With organization-wide dependency search, security teams and developers can quickly locate vulnerable, non-compliant, or otherwise problematic components across their entire codebase without navigating repository by repository. Powered by a rearchitected indexing pipeline, search is fast and reliable even at scale, giving you confidence that results are accurate and complete.

Expected Outcome

Organizations need a fast, trustworthy way to answer the question "where are we using this dependency?" especially when a critical vulnerability or malware advisory drops. The previous Organization Insights experience suffered from performance issues on large repositories and growing inaccuracy as dependency graph shifted to snapshot-based parsing. This release replaces that experience with a purpose-built, high-performance search capability so that customers can identify and remediate supply chain risks across their organization in seconds, not hours.

entry.title: Keyless GitHub App Tokens in Actions [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With keyless GitHub App tokens in Actions, you can securely run workflows that act as a GitHub App without needing to store or manage private keys as secrets. This makes it easier and safer to automate tasks like creating pull requests, managing branches, or accessing private repositories, all while reducing the risk of credential leaks.

Expected Outcome

This update aims to eliminate the need for distributing and storing private keys for GitHub Apps in Actions workflows, tightening security and simplifying setup. By allowing only trusted workflows to mint tokens based on admin-defined policies, customers gain more control and peace of mind over their automation and integrations.

entry.title: Granular Permissions for Repository Secrets and Variables
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now assign permissions for managing repository secrets and variables without giving full write access to your repository. This makes it easy to control who can create, update, or delete sensitive credentials, so your team can collaborate securely while keeping important information protected.

Expected Outcome

By separating secrets and variables management from general write access, organizations can better enforce least-privilege access and reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorized changes to sensitive data. This helps teams maintain strong security and compliance standards without disrupting their regular development workflows.

entry.title: Scoped secrets and reusable workflow improvements [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Scoped secrets let you control exactly where secrets are used, like specific repositories, branches, or workflows. This means reusable workflows get the secrets they need automatically, without extra setup or duplication, making secret management simpler and more secure.

Expected Outcome

By introducing scoped secrets, teams can reduce manual work and avoid spreading secrets across multiple places. Organizations gain better visibility and control over secret usage, supporting safer automation and helping meet compliance and security needs.

entry.title: Locked Dependencies for GitHub Actions Workflows
entry.content:
Value Prop

With workflow-embedded dependency locking in GitHub Actions, you can ensure your CI/CD pipelines always use the exact versions of Actions and dependencies you’ve reviewed. This gives you reproducible builds, clear visibility into changes, and stronger protection against unexpected or compromised code.

Expected Outcome

By making dependency resolution explicit and verifiable, this feature helps teams prevent silent drift and supply chain risks in their workflows. The goal is to improve reliability, security, and confidence in every workflow run, so you can focus on building and shipping with peace of mind.

entry.title: [npm] Support multiple trusted publishing workflows per package [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now set up multiple trusted publishing workflows for each npm package, making it easy to publish stable releases, betas, and other versions from different CI workflows—all without relying on long-lived tokens. This gives you more flexibility and security, letting you use short-lived credentials for every publishing path.

Expected Outcome

By supporting multiple OIDC configurations per package and namespace, teams can fully retire long-lived publish tokens and streamline their release processes. This change aims to improve both the security and convenience of npm publishing for projects with complex or multi-path release workflows.

entry.title: Code scanning alerts link to GitHub Issues to facilitate collaboration and work management [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Security teams and developers can link code scanning alerts directly to GitHub Issues, bringing security remediation into the same collaboration and planning workflows they already use for feature work. Instead of tracking vulnerabilities in spreadsheets or jumping between security tools, teams get native traceability from alert to issue to pull request within GitHub. With GA, this extends to full programmatic access via REST APIs and webhooks, enabling automated triage workflows and integration with existing processes at scale.

Expected Outcome

Shorter time-to-remediation for security findings by removing friction between detection and developer action. Security teams can create actionable issues from alerts, assign them to the right developers, and track progress through existing project boards. Developers see linked security alerts directly on their issues, so they understand the "why" behind the work without switching tools. At GA, API and webhook support lets enterprises build automated pipelines reducing manual triage overhead and ensuring no critical finding falls through the cracks.

entry.title: Dependabot now supports alerting on artifacts and non-default branches [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Dependabot can now generate security alerts for artifacts—such as containers, packages, and executables—as well as dependencies on non-default branches. By uploading a software bill of materials (SBOM) to GitHub's snapshot service and flagging it as alert-worthy, teams gain continuous vulnerability monitoring for every released artifact and long-running branch, not just the default branch. This closes a critical blind spot where production services and shipped products could be silently exposed to newly discovered vulnerabilities in pinned dependency versions.

Expected Outcome

Non-default branch alerting is the most highly requested Dependabot feature in customer feedback. With this release, customers can detect zero-day vulnerabilities in any released artifact or long-lived branch—ensuring that the software they ship and operate stays protected even after the repository has moved on. We expect this to significantly reduce unpatched exposure windows, strengthen end-to-end supply chain security, and reinforce GitHub as the trusted platform for securing the entire software delivery pipeline.

entry.title: Agentic Autofix for Security Alerts in PRs [public preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With agentic autofix, you can automatically resolve code scanning security alerts in pull requests with fixes that are verified for safety and effectiveness. This means you spend less time investigating and validating fixes, and can confidently commit changes knowing they won’t break your code or introduce new vulnerabilities.

Expected Outcome

We want to make it easier and safer for developers to address security issues in their code by providing automated, validated fixes directly within pull requests. This should reduce the time and effort needed to remediate security findings, leading to more secure code and a smoother development workflow.

entry.title: GitHub secret scanning - extended metadata is generally available [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

To help you understand ownership and impact of a leaked secret, GitHub secret scanning now surfaces additional metadata for supported secret types. Metadata varies by type and includes owner-email, owner-id, owner-name, secret-id, secret name, secret-issued-date, secret-expiration-date, organization-name, organization-id, and last-used-date.

Expected Outcome

When a secret is leaked, knowing what was exposed is only half the battle. Teams also need to know who owns it, when it was created, and what systems it can access. This enriched metadata helps teams dramatically reduce the time it takes security and development teams to triage and remediate leaked secrets.

entry.title: Agentic autofix generation for code scanning alerts [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

With agentic autofix for code scanning alerts, users can automatically resolve security issues in their code by assigning alerts to an advanced agent that generates and submits pull requests with fixes. This streamlines the remediation process, saving time and reducing manual effort for development and security teams.

Expected Outcome

By making agentic autofix generally available to all paying GitHub Advanced Security and code security users, more organizations can quickly address vulnerabilities and maintain secure codebases. The goal is to increase the speed and efficiency of fixing code scanning alerts, leading to stronger security and less operational overhead.

entry.title: Attested SBOMs associated with artifacts are now visible in a repository's dependency graph [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Organizations need full visibility into the software dependencies behind every release—not just what's on the default branch today. With attested SBOMs now surfaced in the dependency graph, customers can inspect the exact dependency tree associated with any artifact, giving them a trustworthy, point-in-time view of what shipped. This strengthens supply-chain security posture, supports compliance and audit workflows, and builds confidence that dependency data is accurate and tamper-evident through attestation.

Expected Outcome

Enable customers to store, view, and act on multiple dependency graph snapshots—not just the tip of the default branch. This is critical for teams maintaining long-term-support (LTS) releases or long-running production deployments, where newly-disclosed vulnerabilities against historical dependency trees represent real risk. By making attested SBOMs visible in the dependency graph, we lay the foundation for historical vulnerability alerting and give security teams the tools to assess and remediate risk across every release they support.

entry.title: GitHub Enterprise Server now supports the "one pipeline" framework for dependency graph generation [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Enterprise Server now supports the "one pipeline" framework for dependency graph generation, bringing years of dependency graph platform improvements to GHES customers. This includes transitive dependency resolution, dev dependency labelling, broader ecosystem support, and private registry credential handling — capabilities previously available only on GitHub.com. With this update, GHES customers get a more accurate, comprehensive view of their software supply chain without needing to change their workflows.

Expected Outcome

GHES customers gain parity with GitHub.com's modern dependency graph pipeline, enabling richer dependency insights and stronger supply chain security posture out of the box. By consolidating on the "one pipeline" framework and deprecating legacy generation methods, we reduce platform complexity and ensure all customers benefit from ongoing dependency graph improvements as they ship. This drives deeper adoption of GitHub's supply chain security features across the enterprise segment.

entry.title: Workflow Execution Protections: Actor and Event Configuration [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Workflow execution protections give administrators precise control over which GitHub Actions workflows can run, based on who triggers them and what event starts them. This helps teams prevent unauthorized or unexpected workflow runs, making it easier to safeguard sensitive information and maintain build integrity across all projects.

Expected Outcome

By introducing these protections, organizations can strengthen their security posture and reduce the risk of supply chain attacks or insider threats. Applying consistent, centralized rules for workflow triggers helps teams scale their governance, ensuring only trusted actors and events can execute workflows across repositories.

entry.title: GitHub Code Quality: Org-level quality trends and time-series data [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Code Quality now surfaces org-level trend data so security and engineering leaders can see whether code quality is improving or declining over time — without leaving GitHub. Time-series charts make it easy to spot regressions early, measure the impact of quality initiatives, and communicate progress to stakeholders. Instead of relying on a point-in-time snapshot, teams get a continuous, data-driven view of their codebase health across the organization.

Expected Outcome

Today, the org-level Code Quality dashboard answers "Where do we stand right now?" but not "Are we getting better?" By adding time-series trend data, we enable leaders to track quality trajectories, catch regressions before they compound, and demonstrate ROI on quality investments — all from the security overview they already use. This closes one of the most-requested gaps in the Code Quality experience and is a key milestone on the path to Code Quality GA.
